t.E475.agn: In 2017 EFSA saw no need for a numerical acceptable daily intake (ADI) and found no safety concern at the reported uses. In a 2022 follow-up opinion it recommended tightening the limits for impurities (e.g. toxic elements, 3-MCPD, glycidyl esters).
t.E475.body: Polyglycerol esters are almost completely split in the gut into polyglycerol and fatty acids; absorption in intact form is very low.
t.E475.eval: The fatty acid source may be vegetable or animal (including beef/pork); the source is often not stated on the label.
t.E475.prod: It is an emulsifier produced by esterifying polyglycerol with edible fats and oils or with fatty acids.
t.E475.regx.0: Re-evaluated; no numerical ADI needed, no safety concern at the reported uses.
t.E475.regx.1: Follow-up opinion: lowering of the limits for toxic elements in the specifications and adding limits for erucic acid, 3-MCPD and glycidyl esters were recommended.
t.E475.summary: An emulsifier produced from glycerol and fatty acids. It is used in cakes and bakery products.
t.E475.what: It is an emulsifier; it helps dough hold air and helps fat disperse.
